title: Tilam Angin
subject: sleeping on a friend's living-room floor on an air mattress that goes a little flatter every night, in the month between losing one rented room and finding the next
caption: Malaysian shoegaze in the Kuala Lumpur scene style, sung in Malay. Walls of fuzz guitar run into long reverb, with reverse-reverb swells and tremolo-arm glide bends that pull each chord slightly out of tune; a droning root-note bass holding every chord for a full bar; steady mid-tempo drums with a washy ride and crash, buried low under the guitars. Washed out and very wide, the guitar wash forward, the vocal low and blurred inside it, nothing dry. A breathy female voice, soft and sighing, singing short simple lines just under the guitars. 96 BPM, D major. Drowsy, lonely and oddly calm. No crisp pop vocal on top, no synth arpeggios, no trap drums, no autotune, no dry indie riffing.
lyrics:
[Intro - fuzz guitar swell with reverse reverb]

[Verse 1]
Ruang tamu kawan
Cahaya peti ais
Tilam angin biru
Saya pam lagi

[Pre-Chorus]
Pukul tiga pagi
Bahu cecah lantai

[Chorus]
Perlahan-lahan turun
Setiap malam sikit
Saya tak bangun pam
Lantai pun tak apa

[Verse 2]
Kawan dah tidur
Pintu bilik dia tutup
Beg saya dua
Tepi rak kasut

[Bridge - guitars swell, drums drop out]
Bilik sewa baru
Belum ada lagi

[Chorus]
Perlahan-lahan turun
Setiap malam sikit
Saya tak bangun pam
Lantai pun dah biasa

[Outro - one fuzz chord ringing out]
Tilam angin biru
Dah rata
